chapters.title: Hello
chapters.text: Welcome to Grove! Think of it like a toy machine. You draw a treasure map. Grove freezes that map into a hard brick. Then a little robot reads the brick every frame and makes the game world move.

chapters.title: The main path
chapters.text: Follow the bright path. First you draw. Then the importer makes cards. Then the bake oven freezes everything into one brick called Graph Data. That brick is what play time uses.

chapters.title: Helpers
chapters.text: Two helpers sit beside the path. Numbers on each box pick which door the robot opens. The backpack called Grove State remembers secrets between frames, like inputs and local variables.

chapters.title: Three rooms
chapters.text: There are three rooms. Draw time is Graph Toolkit. Bake time freezes the brick. Play time is your E C S system. Never mix the rooms up. The pretty map is not the brick.

chapters.title: Hello
chapters.text: Welcome to the cooking show. Recipe is your map. Oven is the baker. Dinner plate is the robot tick. Same three steps every time.

chapters.title: Main path
chapters.text: You draw the pretty map. The importer builds an Auth box — a frozen card deck of Root, inputs, outputs, and nodes. Authoring on an entity only points at that Auth box. The bake oven reads the Auth box and freezes a brick. Play never opens the pretty map again.

chapters.title: Start door
chapters.text: The start door rule: exactly one Input wire must touch the first action box. Zero starts or two starts means the importer yells.

chapters.title: Extras
chapters.text: Variants pick a branch while baking, so unpicked paths disappear from the brick. The backpack holds live memory after bake.

chapters.title: What a frame is
chapters.text: A frame is one heartbeat of the game. Your system wakes, hands the robot a remote for this frame, points its bags at a group of entities, then walks the brick starting at Root.

chapters.title: Wake the robot
chapters.text: Get Execution is not a full rebuild. It refreshes generated handles, stamps time and logger into Grove Context, and returns a Graph Execution value. That value is a copy of the context bag for this update.

chapters.title: Walk the brick
chapters.text: Set Chunk first. That aims Component Container and Buffer Container at this Archetype Chunk. Then Execute starts at Root. Each box has a Type number. The door book opens that case and runs a static method.

chapters.title: Side effects and questions
chapters.text: Leaf methods write things like Local Transform. Data boxes sleep until something calls Calculate. If you Set Input first, you wrote a variable into the backpack. The graph reads it later. It is not a stack argument to Root.

chapters.title: Hello
chapters.text: The brick is a sandwich factory. Shell on the outside. Each box is bread plus filling. Little arrows point to kid boxes.

chapters.title: Shell
chapters.text: Outside: Graph Id stamps the backpack keys. Root is the start door. Inputs and Outputs are the labeled holes.

chapters.title: Box
chapters.text: Every node: bread is Type and Node Id. Filling is payload like Speed or score lists. Kids are blob pointers.

chapters.title: Doors
chapters.text: Robot reads Type, opens that door in the door book, runs the method, maybe follows more arrows, maybe writes the world.

chapters.title: Compile vs play
chapters.text: The brick only stores numbers. Someone has to write a book that says what number forty two means. That book is generated when your project compiles, onto your partial Context type.

chapters.title: What it hunts
chapters.text: It finds your partial struct that implements I Context. It finds static methods with Execute Node or Data Node attributes. It also peeks into Grove for public built-in toys like Composite.

chapters.title: What it writes
chapters.text: Create Generated, Update Generated, and Set Chunk Generated wire your component bags. Then big switches: Execution Generated and Data Generated. Debug doors appear only when instrumentation is on.

chapters.title: Play time
chapters.text: Play never invents methods. Header Type selects a case. That case calls your static method with payload rehydrated from bytes after the header. Unknown Type becomes a no-op or default value.

chapters.title: Two play styles
chapters.text: Push starts at Root and walks action boxes. Pull starts at an Output and asks a data box for a value. Most graphs use both: selectors push, but they pull scores on the way.

chapters.title: Push path
chapters.text: Root may enter a Composite that runs every child. A Selector scores options, picks one action, executes it. The leaf finally moves the world. Nothing magic loops the whole brick each frame.

chapters.title: Pull path
chapters.text: Calculate on an Output evaluates only the data chain needed. Variables read the backpack. Qualifiers fold floats. If nothing asks, those boxes stay asleep.

chapters.title: Backpack between frames
chapters.text: Inputs, locals, and state machine ints live in Grove State on the entity. Keys include Graph Id. When one graph ends, remove only that Graph Id's keys so other graphs keep their memory.

queued.text: Root. Push starts here for execution graphs.

planning.text: Composite. Run every connected execution child in order.

executing.text: Selector. Pull scores, push one action.

completed.text: World changed this frame for that entity.

approval.text: An Output or data question. Pull entry.

cancelled.text: Next frame will Get Execution again.

expired.text: Same entity still holds Grove State.

chapters.title: Hello
chapters.text: Every custom toy has four LEGO pieces: data struct, auth card, draw node, and run method. Grove glues them with numbers.

chapters.title: Four pieces
chapters.text: Data holds Speed. Auth serializes it. Draw node is what you see in Graph Toolkit. Run method is the static C sharp with the attribute.

chapters.title: Wire
chapters.text: Importer copies draw fields into auth. Bake packs header plus payload. Use With Graph scopes the node to your map type.

chapters.title: Play
chapters.text: At play, Type hits your case in the door book. Method gets payload, Grove Context, and your context by ref. Then it mutates the world.

chapters.title: Contract
chapters.text: Grove is a three-layer package: Editor authoring, Authoring bake, and runtime execution. You author a Graph Toolkit asset that derives Grove Graph. Import produces a Grove Auth Graph. Baking produces a Blob Asset Reference of Graph Data on an I Graph Reference component. Runtime never reads the source map.

chapters.title: Pipeline
chapters.text: Pipeline: Grove Importer walks I Grove Nodes and subgraphs, sets Root when exactly one Input boundary resolves to an execution node, then Graph Authoring references the auth asset. Graph Baking Setup System reflects I Graph Baking types and creates Graph Baking System of T C. Auth Create builds the blob.

chapters.title: Dispatch and state
chapters.text: Each baked node is a header of Type int plus Node Id, then an inline payload. Execution Header Execute calls context Execution Generated, a source-generated switch. Live graph memory is the Grove State buffer, a dynamic untyped hash map keyed by Graph Id so multi-graph entities do not clobber each other.

chapters.title: Assemblies
chapters.text: Bovine Labs Grove Editor owns Toolkit nodes and import. Grove Authoring owns auth assets and bakers. Grove runtime owns Graph Impl, Graph Execution, built-in nodes, and the source generator contract. Your I System owns one Graph Impl and builds a Graph Execution each update after Set Chunk.

chapters.text: Import and bake are pure authoring. Runtime only consumes Blob Asset Reference Graph Data. Graph Authoring or Graph Authoring Buffer reference Grove Auth Graph, never the source my graph file.

chapters.text: Source GroveGraph is imported by GroveImporter into GroveAuthGraph plus node subassets. GraphAuthoring references the auth main object. GraphBakingSystem calls Auth.Create to emit GraphData. Runtime IGraphReference holds only the blob.

chapters.title: Ownership
chapters.text: Graph Impl is constructed in On Create and lives for the system. Each On Update you call Get Execution, schedule a job or iterate chunks, call Set Chunk once per chunk, then Execute or Calculate per entity index.

chapters.title: GetExecution
chapters.text: Get Execution runs Update Generated then your Update hook. It builds Grove Context with World time and optional B L Logger. Graph Execution is a struct. Assigning Context copies the containers by value for that handle.

chapters.title: SetChunk and Execute
chapters.text: Set Chunk calls Set Chunk Generated then your Set Chunk. Execute no-ops if the blob is not created or Root is invalid. It sets Entity, Entity Index In Chunk, and Graph Id, then Root Value Execute which enters Execution Generated unless Type is Default.

chapters.title: Inputs and Calculate
chapters.text: Try Set Input finds a single Graph Input Data entry whose Type Hash matches T. It writes via Set Variable on the Grove State map. Calculate locates an output by unique type or Variable Key, then evaluates the Data Header chain demand-driven.

chapters.title: Layout
chapters.text: Graph Data is a blob root: Graph Id, Root pointer, Inputs array, Outputs array, Root Nodes and Nodes hash maps of Node Union tags.

chapters.title: Shell
chapters.text: Graph Input Data stores Variable Key and Burst Type Hash. Graph Output Data also stores a Blob Ptr to a Data Header that produces the value.

chapters.title: Header+payload
chapters.text: Header is twelve-ish bytes: int Type, ulong Node Id. Payload is at address of header plus size of header. Same pattern for Execution and Data headers.

chapters.title: Dispatch
chapters.text: Data path special-cases Constant, Variable, Variable Set before Data Generated. Execution always goes through Execution Generated for non-default types.

chapters.title: Generator boundaries
chapters.text: BovineLabs.ContextGenerator skips generating inside BovineLabs.Grove, Grove.Authoring, and Grove.Editor assemblies. Your game assembly is where the partial Context is completed. Referenced public attributed methods from Grove still appear as switch cases.

chapters.title: Discovery rules
chapters.text: Context must be a partial unmanaged struct implementing IContext of Self and exposing GroveStates. Node methods must be static, not in generic outer types, with context by ref. Generic T where T is IContext of T matches every context. Concrete MyContext matches only that one.

chapters.title: Emitted surface
chapters.text: Recognized fields include ComponentContainer, BufferContainer, EnableableContainer, SharedComponentContainer, ComponentLookup, BufferLookup, EntityStorageInfoLookup. Emit also covers debug methods under UNITY_INCLUDE_INSTRUMENTATION.

chapters.title: Call path
chapters.text: ExecutionHeader.Execute calls ExecutionGenerated. DataHeader.Calculate special-cases Default, Constant, Variable, VariableSet, then DataGenerated. Payload is recovered with pointer arithmetic after the header size.

user.text: Your runtime assembly with partial MyContext and node classes.

chapters.title: No full interpreter
chapters.text: Runtime is recursive descent through blob pointers. Execute pushes control flow. Calculate pulls expressions. There is no system that visits every node each frame.

chapters.title: Built-in control flow
chapters.text: CompositeData holds a BlobArray of ExecutionHeader pointers. Selectors keep parallel Qualifier and Action arrays; the last pair is the default threshold path; win conditions use strict greater-than on floats.

chapters.title: Data evaluation
chapters.text: Outputs bind to DataHeaders. Variable and VariableSet are special-cased before generated dispatch. VariableSet re-evaluates and writes on every Calculate of its output.

chapters.title: GroveState keys
chapters.text: GroveStateKey includes GraphId, optional scope, and key material from Hash128 splits for variables. GraphStateUtil.RemoveGraphState iterates keys and removes those with matching GraphId.

completed.text: ECS mutations already applied this tick.

chapters.title: Split
chapters.text: Split across assemblies: unmanaged payload and enums in data or runtime, Grove Execution Auth or Data Auth in Authoring, Grove Execution Node in Editor, static Execute Node method in runtime.

chapters.title: Pieces
chapters.text: Auth Node Type returns your enum int. Init writes blob fields via Blob Remap Builder. Editor Init copies inspector fields onto auth during import.

chapters.title: Bake
chapters.text: Create Node on auth allocates header and payload in the graph blob. Instance overrides patch serializable fields per entity before Create. Add Dependencies tracks extra assets.

chapters.title: Dispatch
chapters.text: Attribute Execute Node type id must match baked Type. Signature is public or internal static, non-generic outer type, ref context. Optional typed input for context and block nodes.
